TABLE 26-7  Risk of Nutritional Deficiency
Level of Risk
Food Characteristics/Examples
Low risk
Any food that can easily be eliminated with minimum or no nutritional risk to the patient; substitutes are easily incorporated 
into the diet; protein, fat, calorie and nutrient consumption is optimal.
Example: Avoidance of a specific fruit or vegetable or tree nuts
Moderate risk
Any food that may be encountered frequently throughout the food supply, yet the elimination of which does not significantly 
limit food choices or vital nutrient sources; adequacy of protein, fat, calorie, and nutrient consumption need monitoring.
Example: Avoidance of soy, fish, or eggs
High risk
Any food or usually group of foods that permeates the food supply, providing a significant source of specific nutrients  
that are not readily available through other foods that are a part of the normal diet; the elimination of which results in a 
significant lifestyle and dietary change because of the difficulty of avoiding that food and products containing that food; 
adequate protein, fat, calorie, and nutrient consumption unlikely; nutrient supplementation often necessary.
Example: Avoidance of wheat, soy, egg, cow’s milk, fish, or multiple foods
